summary: MerchantEdge: session parity loss causing long-tail 5xxs and streaming fallback loop — post-incident follow-up
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 03:10–03:45 UTC, MerchantEdge experienced elevated 5xx rates and repeated streaming disconnects. Customers reported truncated responses and repeated retry-triggered fallback requests that amplified load. The initial symptom was a rising tail latency on streaming sessions, then a cascade of 502/504 and a client-observed fallback loop.
timeline:
2026-03-10 03:08 UTC: MerchantEdge support contact via #support-merchantedge.
2026-03-10 03:12 UTC: SRE triage declared incident and began traffic routing to secondary region.
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC: Observed increased error rate on streaming-proxy and smart-routing logs indicating session-state mismatch.
2026-03-10 03:27 UTC: Canary rollback of kernel-selection PR and temporary disablement of enhanced KV-cache routing applied for affected hosts.
2026-03-10 03:36 UTC: Error rate returned to baseline; streaming sessions stabilized.
2026-03-10 04:00 UTC: Declared major incident mitigated.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC: Post-incident review and follow-up actions documented.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a long-running streaming session with stateful tool-calls and a sequence of >512 token prefixes.
2) Route requests through smart-routing policy 'latency-prefer' with prefix-KV caching enabled.
3) Trigger concurrent reconnections from the client (simulated network jitter).
4) Observe eventual 502s from streaming-proxy when session token IDs misalign and fallback routing issues cause duplicate inflight requests.

investigation_notes: Hypotheses tested: 1) Kernel-selection PR introduced a perf path that changed sequence-number assignment for quantized kernels under certain batch sizes. 2) Smart-routing's prefix-aware KV-cache returned an out-of-sync KV snapshot when sessions reattached to a different host. Evidence: repeated 'session-mismatch' WARNs and 'inconsistent-kv-length' errors in serving-runtime logs. Confirmed by correlating request IDs across proxy and runtime logs and replaying with client jitter in staging. Linked instrumentation traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/INC-91234. Root cause narrowed to race between session-resume handler and KV-cache population code when a session migrated between hosts during enhanced kernel path selection.
root_cause: Race condition in session-resume + KV-cache population interacting with an in-flight kernel-selection change. Under transient client reconnects, sessions could resume with stale sequence metadata, causing serving-runtime to reject requests (5xx) and triggering fallback routing that multiplied inflight attempts.
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation: rolled back kernel-selection change on canary and then full cluster (2026-03-10 03:27–03:33 UTC); disabled prefix-aware KV-cache routing temporarily for affected host pool; blocked smart-routing policy 'latency-prefer' from selecting quantized-hosts during customer sessions. Long-term fix: apply synchronization to session-resume handler, add validation and retry on KV-cache mismatch, and add unit/integration tests for session migration + jitter. Deployed hotfix branch serving-runtime@pr-2193-fix on 2026-03-11 and scheduled full rollout during low-traffic window 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC.
